UnitStatement: The DIRECTIVE document captures the founding intent, design philosophy, professional responsibility model, and structural constraints for Chirality App; it is the "why" document.
CONTRACT.md, SPEC.md, TYPES.md, PLAN.md, agent instructions, implementation code, execution deliverables, and release runbooks must remain consistent with the directive.
Where implementation conflicts with the directive, implementation is incomplete or nonconforming until a governed change updates the relevant record.
The governing document set is read as a coherent system in a defined authority order.
DIRECTIVE.md defines intent, values, and structural commitments.
CONTRACT.md defines binding invariants.
SPEC.md defines physical structures, file formats, runtime mechanics, and validation surfaces.
TYPES.md defines vocabulary, identifiers, enums, and type targets.
PLAN.md defines the development roadmap and sequencing rationale.
docs/PRD.md states current product requirements and the accepted implementation direction.
AGENTS.md, agents/AGENT_*.md, accepted execution deliverables, scope-change records, and release runbooks constrain concrete operations.
If a lower-authority artifact conflicts with a higher-authority governance source, the higher-authority source controls until a governed change updates the record.
The PRD establishes vNext product direction but does not erase the authority of the directive, contract, specification, vocabulary, accepted execution scope, or professional-boundary commitments.
Chirality is a local-first desktop harness for running governed AI agents against a user-selected filesystem workspace.
Chirality bundles a release-managed instruction root inside the app, lets the user select a mutable working root, and uses plain files plus git history as the durable substrate for professional work.
Core insight: if the filesystem is the database, architecture is a state-and-authority specification, not a service mesh.
Chirality exists to accelerate deliverable-heavy professional work by organizing agent activity around packages, deliverables, dependencies, lifecycle files, and review gates.
Chirality exists to make AI-assisted work auditable, reviewable, and controllable where provenance, human accountability, and traceability matter.
Chirality exists to keep humans in charge of every binding decision while agents perform drafting, extraction, reconciliation, scaffolding, summarization, and routine transformation.
Chirality exists to provide a desktop harness whose product identity is Chirality, not a vendor CLI, SDK, cloud workflow, or hidden database.
Chirality exists to preserve a path from interactive assistance to governed deliverable production without implying automated professional approval.

Chirality is not just a chat wrapper; it is a governed work harness combining local filesystem truth, agent instructions, deterministic tools, runtime auditability, human gates, and a professional-responsibility posture.
Project state is represented as human-readable files under the working root, with no required external database, hidden server, or vendor-hosted project memory.
Nodes are package folders, deliverable folders, domain profile folders, proposal folders, and tool-root snapshots.
Edges are Dependencies.csv rows, lifecycle references, traceability references, operation proposals, and review records.

Properties are markdown and CSV files such as _STATUS.md, _CONTEXT.md, _DEPENDENCIES.md, _REFERENCES.md, Dependencies.csv, Datasheet.md, Specification.md, Guidance.md, Procedure.md, and session event logs.
Agents and tools may traverse filesystem state but do not replace it; when a fact matters for reliance, it must land in the appropriate versioned project file or approved artifact.

Git history is the durable event store for accepted project state, providing reviewable diffs, rollback, traceability, and auditability independent of chat history, vendor transcripts, runtime caches, or UI state.
If a decision is not in a versioned file, it does not exist for purposes of reliance.
Runtime session logs explain what happened during agent work and are important audit records, but are not a substitute for accepted project-state files and human approval records.

Chirality runtime events record accepted turns, provider/SDK messages, model deltas, permission decisions, tool calls, hook outcomes, compaction boundaries, subagent lifecycle, failures, interruptions, and terminal outcomes, supporting replay, diagnosis, and review.
The canonical Chirality runtime audit mirror is .chirality/sessions/<sessionId>/events.jsonl or an explicitly configured Chirality-controlled session path.
External SDK transcripts are secondary runtime artifacts unless imported into Chirality's event schema.
Runtime events do not make a deliverable approved, issued, code-compliant, externally validated, or safe for reliance.
Gate-relevant decisions must be represented in versioned project files and accepted by an accountable human.
Agents propose; humans approve. Professional responsibility is personal, non-transferable, and not delegated to a model, tool, SDK, runtime, or deterministic validator.

Only humans may author binding approval records, approve issue/release actions, select governing standards, accept residual risk, adjudicate source conflicts requiring judgment, and decide whether work may be relied upon.
Approvals bind to specific content and must be traceable to a git SHA or equivalent immutable evidence; content changes after approval void the approval until reviewed again.
Chirality values evidence over fluent output and must prefer source-backed statements, explicit assumptions, and visible uncertainty over plausible invention.
Required posture: cite or record source paths for extracted dependencies and important claims.
Required posture: label assumptions as ASSUMPTION, proposals as PROPOSAL, unknowns as TBD, and observed facts as FACT where practical.
Required posture: surface conflicts rather than silently resolving them.
Required posture: prefer 'location TBD' over fabricated provenance.
Required posture: use deterministic tools for validation, parsing, scaffolding, linting, and repeatable transformations when available.

No hidden memory may become authoritative project state; UI drafts, local presets, SDK transcripts, model context, runtime logs, app caches, API keys, and provider transcripts are non-authoritative unless a governed process imports their content into the project filesystem.

Convenience state is permitted when explicitly non-authoritative and unable to override governance; examples include UI pane widths, local runtime presets, API key storage, draft chat text, and SDK resume metadata.
Chirality separates the release-managed instruction root from the mutable working root.

The instruction root is bundled app resources such as AGENTS.md, agents/, docs/, framework guidance, and release-managed instructions; it is read-only during ordinary project execution and updated only by release/governance changes.

The working root (projectRoot) is the user-selected local filesystem path where project execution state, deliverables, sessions, and tool artifacts live; it is mutable under runtime policy and human gates.
The instruction root defines how agents should behave; the working root contains the project being worked on; these roots must not be conflated.
Chirality should use a provider-adapter runtime architecture for generic agent-loop mechanics where an external provider or SDK satisfies Chirality requirements behind product-owned contracts.
The Claude Agent SDK / Anthropic path is the first concrete adapter and current shipped path.

Provider/SDK adapters may provide the model/tool loop, built-in file tools, bash surface, permission-mode machinery, hook dispatch, MCP transport, SDK transcripts, subagent invocation, and compaction messages.
Provider/SDK adapters do not own Chirality's product contract.
Chirality owns AgentEnginePort / RuntimeEngineContract.
Chirality owns the browser UIEvent and persisted HarnessEvent schemas.
Chirality owns session canonicality and the Chirality audit mirror.
Chirality owns permission semantics, capability policy, and explicit hard-deny precedence.
Chirality owns working-root and instruction-root policy.
Chirality owns persona/system-prompt composition.
Chirality owns _STATUS.md and Dependencies.csv lifecycle rules.
Chirality owns subagent governance.
Chirality owns path containment, redaction, and provenance.
Chirality owns professional-boundary language.
Chirality owns user-facing product identity.
Chirality owns fallback criteria if SDK behavior cannot be governed.
The preferred architecture is provider-adapter-general, contract-owned, and Chirality-governed.
A reliance boundary is a product-critical semantic determining whether a user can trust the harness to preserve safety, auditability, authority, or professional boundaries.

Examples of reliance boundaries include path containment, instruction-root protection, accepted-turn persistence, human-gate enforcement, transcript canonicality, permission denial, subagent gating, and settings isolation.
Reliance boundaries must be documented, implemented, and tested in Chirality terms and must not depend on prompt text or opaque SDK defaults alone.
When SDK hooks or callbacks enforce a boundary, Chirality must be able to verify the enforcement path and record the result.
The runtime engine may be difficult to replace in practice but must be replaceable by construction.
Public APIs, canonical event schemas, session storage contracts, permission decision records, and governance rules must not become SDK-shaped.
External identifiers, message names, permission modes, tool names, transcript paths, and SDK session IDs are adapter metadata; Chirality contracts remain provider-neutral and product-owned.
Chirality may use external engines, libraries, and APIs but must not become a Claude Code wrapper in identity, copy, behavior, or governance.

User-facing text should describe Chirality's governed-work posture; SDK usage may be disclosed as implementation/provider detail but must not imply Chirality is Claude Code, an Anthropic product, or a feature-parity target.
The Professional Responsibility Model applies when Chirality is used for safety-significant, contractually binding, regulated, professional, or high-stakes deliverables.
Agent outputs are drafts and structured assistance; they are not authoritative engineering judgment, professional approval, or certification.
Human acceptance is what may turn an output into project work product.
A licensed or accountable professional retains decision rights for scope and boundary decisions.
A licensed or accountable professional retains decision rights for design basis and governing code/standard selection.
A licensed or accountable professional retains decision rights for assumptions and residual-risk acceptance.
A licensed or accountable professional retains decision rights for conflict adjudication where judgment is required.
A licensed or accountable professional retains decision rights for issuance, signature, seal, transmittal, or release for reliance.
No AI system, agent, tool, SDK, transcript, runtime event, or deterministic validator may claim to certify, approve, sign, seal, issue, or externally validate professional work.
A professional must not use an agent for work they cannot adequately review.
Using AI assistance that cannot be checked against professional knowledge, source documents, deterministic validation, or appropriate peer review is a competence failure.
In technical and professional matters, agents and users follow a hierarchy of authority.
Hierarchy of authority level 1: laws and regulations.
Hierarchy of authority level 2: codes and standards.
Hierarchy of authority level 3: approved project specifications, design basis, and scope records.
Hierarchy of authority level 4: verified analysis and published sources.
Hierarchy of authority level 5: professional judgment.
Agent outputs carry no independent professional authority; they are decision support until accepted by an accountable human through a governed process.
Chirality supports local desktop operation over a selected working root.
Chirality supports matrix navigation across PORTAL, WORKBENCH, and PIPELINE.
Chirality supports working-root validation, file-tree browsing, and deliverable scanning.
Chirality supports harness sessions, streamed turns, interrupts, runtime options, and attachments.
Chirality supports instruction-root packaging and integrity verification.
Chirality supports API key handling as non-project convenience state.
Chirality supports current Anthropic provider access under governed network policy.
Chirality supports provider/SDK-hosted runtime integration behind Chirality contracts.
Chirality supports append-only Chirality session event logs.
Chirality supports persona/system-prompt composition from instruction-root resources.
Chirality supports status and dependency contract APIs.
Chirality supports execution-root scaffolding.
Chirality supports read tools and Chirality MCP tools under capability policy with explicit hard-deny precedence.
Chirality supports controlled write/edit/bash/subagent capability only after required gates land.
Chirality supports validation and packaging runbooks.
Chirality supports future Domain Engine Profiles after core harness stability.
Chirality does not approve, sign, seal, certify, issue, or transmit professional work autonomously.
Chirality does not make safety-critical decisions without human review.
Chirality does not conduct financial transactions or binding commitments.
Chirality does not require a project database or remote project server.
Chirality does not treat SDK transcripts, runtime logs, UI state, API keys, or chat drafts as project truth.
Chirality does not load ambient user/global Claude Code settings in shipped builds.
Chirality does not use bypassPermissions in shipped builds or ordinary operator workflows.
Chirality does not expose bash, remote MCP, plugins, marketplace extensions, or remote execution before local SDK governance, hooks, event logging, result storage, and packaging checks are reliable.
Chirality does not reactivate retired PKG-08 deliverables without governed amendment.
Chirality does not become OpenPipeStress or any domain-specific solver.
Chirality does not let agents write directly into protected domain-engine model paths.
Structural constraint: local-first desktop harness, so users retain control of project files and working roots.
Structural constraint: no external project database dependency, so project truth stays inspectable, git-trackable, and portable.
Structural constraint: plain-file project state, so humans and tools can inspect, diff, archive, and recover state without the app.
Structural constraint: git-backed reliance record, so accepted project decisions bind to versioned files, not transient chats.
Structural constraint: instruction root separate from working root, so release-managed agent instructions cannot be silently mutated by project execution.
Structural constraint: flat package to deliverable hierarchy, which simplifies decomposition, scanning, coverage checks, and lifecycle contracts.
Structural constraint: deliverable-local dependency registers, so dependencies remain near the work item with on-demand aggregation.
Structural constraint: append-only runtime event log, so accepted turns and runtime outcomes are recoverable after interruption or failure.
Structural constraint: Chirality audit mirror is canonical for runtime governance; SDK transcripts may assist resume/debugging but do not displace product-owned events.
Structural constraint: SDK behind product-owned contract, so upstream behavior cannot silently redefine Chirality semantics.
Structural constraint: shipped SDK settings isolation, so ambient .claude or user-home settings cannot alter shipped harness behavior.
Structural constraint: deny-first permission semantics, so a deny from policy, hook, path check, governance, or human gate overrides any allow.
Structural constraint: runtime code enforces safety; prompt instructions reinforce policy but are not sufficient enforcement.
Structural constraint: MCP is a transport, not a bypass; in-process MCP tools must pass through the same policy as SDK built-ins.
Structural constraint: product identity stays Chirality; the app must not present itself as a vendor CLI or external product.
Structural constraint: domain engines own domain truth; Chirality governs interaction and records but does not become the solver.
Users and maintainers must treat agent outputs as drafts until reviewed.
Users and maintainers must preserve source paths, evidence, and explicit uncertainty.
Users and maintainers must keep human review and sign-off at decision gates.
Users and maintainers must inspect diffs before accepting project-file changes.
Users and maintainers must understand the configured permission mode and tool surface before enabling writes or bash.
Users and maintainers must keep API keys and secrets out of project files and runtime event payloads.
Users and maintainers must verify packaging, instruction-root integrity, and SDK settings isolation before release.
Users and maintainers must maintain professional-boundary copy in UI and documentation.

Changes that alter scope, release target, data contracts, professional-boundary posture, runtime engine semantics, permission behavior, transcript canonicality, or retired/active execution scope must be handled as governed product changes.
A change is not complete until reflected in the appropriate combination of PRD, directive, contract, specification, type vocabulary, plan, tests, runbooks, and implementation artifacts.
